newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Rebel chief leaves Sierra Leone after seeing his men.
newsitem.headline: Rebel chief leaves Sierra Leone after seeing his men.

text.p: Rebel leader Foday Sankoh left Sierra Leone for Ivory Coast on Wednesday after a visit to explain to his commanders the details of a peace deal, the International Committee of the Red Cross said.

A Red Cross spokesman in Ivory Coast's commercial capital Abidjan told Reuters that Sankoh had been flown by helicopter to Guinea from his Revolutionary United Front (RUF) jungle headquarters and then left by plane for Abidjan.
It was not immediately clear whether Sankoh, who took up arms in 1991, had won a mandate from his forces for him to sign a peace deal with President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
Officials in Sierra Leone said last week that the plan was to sign a peace deal in Ivory Coast this Friday.
Tejan Kabbah, who took office in March after multi-party elections ended four years of army rule, earlier threatened the military option if Sankoh did not agree to peace by December 1.
Tejan Kabbah and Sankoh extended a truce indefinitely in April during talks in Ivory Coast following Kabbah's election but failed to agree a definitive peace settlement.
Sankoh had been in Ivory Coast since then but the fragile truce came under strain with mutual accusation of violations.
Differences over the presence of foreign troops -- Nigerians, Guineans and mercenaries from a private South African security firm -- blocked progress towards a peace deal.
The civil war in Sierra Leone, a former British colony, has killed at least 10,000 people, according to official estimates.
